title: Microsoft Teams: change the background while recording a video clip on iPhone
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, messaging-policy path, PowerShell command and general Teams licensing statements match the sources checked. No actionable factual errors were found; the background option's undocumented default and feature-specific controls remain appropriately qualified.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for changing the background while recording this phone video clip.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "background while recording"; "Teams" "clip" "background" "record". Opened Government Channel release notes, messaging policies, meeting audio/video policies and custom meeting backgrounds; no dedicated clip-background page found.

claims.claim: Government Channel release notes describe Video clip as recording, reviewing, sending and viewing short-form video in Teams chat from desktop and mobile.
claims.quote: Video clip is a new feature in Microsoft Teams that enables the user to record, review, send, and view short-form video in Teams chat from desktop and mobile.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].governs; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Video messages messaging-policy setting governs whether users can send video messages in chats and channels, without a background-specific exception.
claims.quote: Video messages - Turn this setting on if you want users in your organization to be able to use the Teams app to send video messages to other people in chats and channels.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The control is at Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Edit > Video messages.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Messaging policies. Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowVideoMessages $true to enable video messages in that policy.
claims.quote: -AllowVideoMessages: This setting determines if users can create and send video messages. Possible values: True, False. -Identity: Identity for the teams messaging policy you're modifying.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Messaging policies are assigned to users, so different assigned policies can produce different messaging capabilities.
claims.quote: Messaging policies are used to control which chat and channel messaging features are available to users (owners and members) in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Users automatically receive the global messaging policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users in your organization will automatically get the global policy, unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one messaging policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can only be assigned one messaging policy at a time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says Teams does not screen images users upload as meeting backgrounds.
claims.quote: Teams doesn't screen the images your users upload. When you use the All video effects setting, you should have internal organization policies to prevent users from uploading offensive or inappropriate images

claims.claim: Participants can use video effects is documented as controlling users' video-background customization in meetings.
claims.quote: Participants can use video effects. This is a per-user policy. This setting controls whether users can customize their video background in a meeting.

claims.claim: Learn does not document a separate setting for the phone clip's background option itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video clip" "background" "policy" "VideoFiltersMode"; "Teams" "background while recording". Opened messaging policies, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy, meeting audio/video policies and custom meeting backgrounds; no clip-background switch found.

claims.claim: The checked documentation does not establish whether meeting video-effects or customization policies govern clip backgrounds.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video clip" "background" "policy" "VideoFiltersMode". Opened meeting-policies-audio-and-video and custom-meeting-backgrounds: both describe meetings/events, not recorded chat clips.

claims.claim: Whether equivalent background-image screening applies to clips is not documented in the checked sources.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video clips" "background" "screen" "sign-in"; "Teams" "clip" "background" "record". Opened meeting audio/video policies, custom meeting backgrounds and Government Channel notes; screening passage concerns meeting backgrounds.

claims.claim: The roadmap and checked Learn documentation describe no identity or sign-in change for this background option.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video clips" "background" "screen" "sign-in". Read roadmap description, messaging policies, Government Channel clip entry and service description; no feature-specific identity or sign-in change found.
